introduction: New Hampshire SNAP applications use NH EASY, with paper, office and phone alternatives described in the state’s application material. Complete the interview and case-specific proof requests.

sections.who: Eligibility considers household size, income, expenses and resources. Having a job, owning a home or living alone does not automatically disqualify you. Housing, utility, medical and child-care deductions may matter. Some adults face work and time-limit rules; ask DHHS to assess an exemption rather than relying on an older age table.
sections.get: Approved food benefits are loaded monthly to EBT. The award depends on the household assessment and is used at authorized retailers.
sections.docs:
• Income and benefit statements.
  • Housing and utility records.
  • Household composition and requested resource information.
  • Other proof listed by the Family Services Specialist.
sections.apply:
1. Submit an application

    Use NH EASY or request a mailed application at 603-271-9700 or 800-852-3345, extension 9700.

  2. Complete the interview

    Keep the appointment or promptly request rescheduling. Explain expenses and circumstances relevant to your household.

  3. Send the requested proof

    Use the worker’s specific list and deadline. Keep copies and confirm receipt.
sections.after:
Read approval, reporting and recertification instructions. NH Food Bank offers application assistance at 877-347-7627, but DHHS makes eligibility decisions.

Ask whether your household qualifies for ESAP: all adults must be 65 or older and/or disabled, with no adult working. Eligible cases have a 36-month certification period and simplified renewal. Report any expense changes requested in the yearly reminder.
sections.sources: Reviewed October 1, 2026 using current DHHS SNAP eligibility and application guidance, state application checklist and NH Food Bank application help. USA Assistance background guide.

faqs: Can I get help completing the application?
NH Food Bank lists a SNAP assistance number, 877-347-7627.
Must I supply every document mentioned in a general brochure?
Use the specialist’s case-specific checklist and ask about alternatives for unavailable records.
Are older work-rule age summaries reliable?
Rules have changed. Ask DHHS for the requirements and exceptions applying to your current case.
Can I apply if I work?
Yes. Employment alone does not rule out SNAP; the agency assesses your household income and other eligibility conditions.
It simplifies SNAP renewal for qualifying older or disabled households with no working adult. Ask DHHS whether your household qualifies.
